text:
Maya R: heads-up — we're getting a spike of 500s and connection timeouts hitting /v1/generate in hosted this morning. Customer support just escalated a paid customer (acme-inc) with repeated failures. seeing ~30% 5xx rate for the last 15m.
Drew (oncall): looking now. any error body samples?
Maya R: logs attached in the console link (https://console.redwood.example/incidents/1719001111). sample: 
```
{"status":500,"error":"gateway_error","message":"upstream read timeout"}
```
Maya R: also seeing a bunch of 502/504 from api-gateway -> runtime pool.
Support Bot: :rotating_light: Alert: hosted-api 5xx-rate > 20% for route /v1/generate in region us-east-1. Triggered at 2026-03-14T09:15:11Z.
Drew (oncall): checking runtime pool sizes and recent deploys. infra any deploys in last hour?
Infra SRE: we rolled a small nginx timeout tweak at 08:50 UTC (commit ea3f7c2) to lower upstream_keepalive to 60s -> trying to reduce idle connections.
Ali K: that change sounds suspicious. upstream_keepalive reduction could cause more TCP churn and new connections, exposing a connection pool exhaustion bug.
Jen S: customers also report auth failures intermittently — are those 401 or 5xx?
Maya R: mostly 5xx, but a subset show 401 for token validation microservice. looks correlated to /v1/generate traffic spikes.
Drew (oncall): I'm seeing runtime nodes returning 500 quickly with logs showing "kv-cache: conn refused" and host limits on fd open. possible file descriptor leak.
Ryan P: can we temporarily divert traffic to fallback models / smaller instances to reduce load?
Drew (oncall): yes. I'll update routing policy to fallback to model-redwood-small-1 for non-enterprise orgs and add per-org throttling. Doing now.
Support Bot: config change applied to routing-policy (rollout id rp-778) — fallback enabled.
Maya R: after the fallback we see 5xx rate drop to ~6% in 10m. customer Acme still has some failures but far fewer.
Drew (oncall): mitigation notes: 1) rolled routing fallback; 2) increased runtime pool in us-east by 30% (spin-up in progress); 3) raised gateway upstream timeouts back to previous value.
Ali K: I'm going to revert the nginx commit and open a ticket to investigate conn-pool FD leak.
Infra SRE: revert pushed (commit ea3f7c2 reverted by ea9b1f0) — monitoring for stability.
Maya R: customer update posted by Support: "we deployed a fallback and are investigating; some requests may be slower; working on permanent fix" :thumbsup:
Drew (oncall): reproduction steps so we can root cause: 
1) reproduce with a high-concurrency synthetic load against /v1/generate (~300 req/s) with 1k token responses;
2) ensure Authorization header present (token for non-enterprise org) to exercise auth proxy;
3) run for 10-15 minutes and tail runtime logs.
Example curl: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer test_abc" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"model-redwood-large","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Drew (oncall): initial hypothesis: nginx timeout change + increased connection churn exposed a FD leak in runtime's KV cache client. when FDs hit limit, auth proxy calls to tokenservice fail intermittently (-> 5xx), and upstream reads time out.
Ali K: created ticket RED-4123: "runtime kv-client FD leak investigation" and assigned to Drew.
Jen S: adding an action item to update runbook: add quick rollback steps for gateway timeouts, include fallback routing recipe and how to throttle large orgs.
Ryan P: I'll add a dashboard for per-org token-exchange latency and a circuit-breaker alert for >10% tokenservice failure across any region.
Maya R: can we get a short postmortem timeline and owner assignments here?
Drew (oncall): timeline (brief):
- 08:50 UTC: nginx timeout change deployed
- 09:10 UTC: token-exchange latency spikes; support tickets start
- 09:15 UTC: automated 5xx alert (Support Bot)
- 09:20 UTC: war room created; routing fallback enabled
- 09:25 UTC: increased runtime pool and reverted nginx change
- 09:35 UTC: 5xx rate dropped to acceptable levels
Action items (owners + ETA):
- RED-4123 (Drew) - investigate FD leak, reproduce locally, deliver patch: ETA 2026-03-21
- Update gateway playbook (Jen S) - add rollback and verification steps: ETA 2026-03-17
- Per-org throttling guidelines (Maya R + Ryan P) - define SLOs and default throttles: ETA 2026-03-18
- Add dashboard & alerts (Ryan P) - token-exchange latency dashboard + circuit-breaker alert: ETA 2026-03-19
- Postmortem doc (Maya R) - draft and circulate to eng+support: ETA 48h (2026-03-16)
Maya R: assigning owners in Asana and linking tickets here.
Support Bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-311 with severity P2.
Ali K: long-term: we'll add a FD sanitizer and better connection pool metrics in runtime. Also plan to fuzz auth proxy under high churn.
Jen S: will update the runbook and push to docs.redwood/team/playbooks/gateway.md.
Drew (oncall): immediate follow-ups I took: pushed temporary limit on per-org concurrency (max 120 concurrent reqs), rolled back nginx change, ramped up runtime pool, and added a short-term scrubbing cron to free stale KV client handles.
Maya R: thanks everyone. posting a customer-facing summary and internal postmortem plan now.
Ryan P: :thumbsup: keep monitoring, will validate dashboards when available.
Drew (oncall): marking this thread as ongoing until RED-4123 is closed.
Maya R: closing war room at 10:15 UTC after metrics stabilized. will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
